sources.title: The Catacomb Cultures of the North-West Caspian Steppe: chronology, reservoir effect, and paleodiet
sources.note: Peer reviewed regional chronology and paired bone dating study; aquatic diets can make human bone dates appear too old.

sources.title: Catacomb culture wagons of the Eurasian steppes
sources.note: Open scholarly monograph covering regional groups, settlement evidence, burials, wagons, economy, social interpretation, and evidentiary limits.

sources.title: Catacomb culture wagons of the Eurasian steppes
sources.note: Peer reviewed Antiquity article documenting complete and partial wheeled vehicles in Catacomb burial contexts and their placement.

sources.title: Ancestry and identity in Bronze Age Catacomb culture burials
sources.note: Peer reviewed East Manych chronology, two sampled males, burial hierarchy methods, Yamnaya overlap, and post-Catacomb transition cautions.

sources.title: Radiocarbon chronology of the Kalmykia Catacomb culture
sources.note: Antiquity study on calibration and development of western Eurasian Catacomb traditions.

sources.title: Ancient human genome-wide data from a 3000-year interval in the Caucasus
sources.note: Open Nature Communications study distinguishing steppe and mountain ancestry profiles, Catacomb samples, and post-Catacomb horizons.

sources.title: The rise and transformation of Bronze Age pastoralists in the Caucasus
sources.note: Nature study of 131 people and 84 dates showing long genetic stability during peak Early and Middle Bronze Age pastoral expansion, followed by later transformation.

sources.title: Ceramics and seasonality: mobile lifeways and ceramic production of the Catacomb population
sources.note: Peer reviewed Lower Don study of summer and early autumn camps, local replacement pottery, and geochemically different ritual vessels.

sources.title: Isotopic perspectives on pastoral practices in the Eastern European forest-steppe
sources.note: Open peer reviewed Ksizovo-1 study of cattle and sheep or goat teeth, regional mobility, forage, and managed birth seasons.

sources.title: The seasonal cycle of grassland use in the Caspian Sea steppe
sources.note: European Journal of Archaeology study of seasonal use of river valleys, uplands, open steppe, and sustainable pastoral movement.

sources.title: Plant food subsistence in Bronze Age Caspian and Low Don steppe pastoralists
sources.note: Peer reviewed pot residue study finding wild plants and barley in funerary contexts while rejecting proof of local farming.

sources.title: Diet and subsistence in Bronze Age pastoral communities from the southern Russian steppes
sources.note: Open PLOS study of human and animal isotopes, varied diets, graves, ornaments, wagons, healed injuries, and regional subsistence.

sources.title: Copper and bronze ornaments in Early and Middle Bronze Age steppe burials
sources.note: National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine study of forged plates, beads, hoops, garment positions, and regional differences.

sources.title: Metal smelting and casting at Catacomb settlements in the forest-steppe Don region
sources.note: Russian Archaeology study of copper and bronze smelting and casting tools at Ksizovo-1 and comparable settlements.

sources.title: Metallurgical Production in Northern Eurasia in the Bronze Age
sources.note: Open Archaeopress study of ores, production evidence, alloying, typical knives, and limits created by uneven investigation.

sources.title: Flint artefacts of northern Pontic Catacomb communities
sources.note: Academic open volume on flint tools and manufacturing kits found in Catacomb burial complexes.

sources.title: The Catacomb culture in the Middle Dniester area
sources.note: Academic regional study of burial construction, grave markers, local distribution, and Middle Dniester chronology.

sources.title: The Ingul-Donets Early Bronze Age cultural landscape
sources.note: Academic synthesis distinguishing western Ingul-Dnieper and eastern Donets traditions, grave forms, settlements, pottery, and research history.

sources.title: Seasonal settlements of the Middle Don Catacomb culture
sources.note: Published landscape study placing winter shelters on floodlands and summer camps on higher terraces, with cattle prominent.

sources.title: Modelling the subsistence economy of the settlement Rykan-3
sources.note: Academy journal study reconstructing a winter cattle-breeding settlement from a single Middle Don Catacomb layer.

sources.title: Anthropological materials from children’s Catacomb burials reviewed
sources.note: Kalmyk Scientific Center study finding that sampled child burials used broadly comparable grave structures and accompaniments to adult burials.

sources.title: Weapons in women’s burials of the Catacomb community
sources.note: National University of Kyiv-Mohyla Academy repository study documenting weapons in women’s graves, especially in the Ingul tradition.

sources.title: Case study of skull trauma treatment in an Inhul Catacomb burial
sources.note: Ukrainian archaeology case study of a healed depressed injury and probable cranial intervention on one adult man.

sources.title: Cemento-osseous dysplasia in a female Bronze Age skeleton
sources.note: Open paleopathology case report identifying a rare jaw condition in an East Manych Catacomb woman without claiming ancient diagnosis or treatment.

sources.title: X-ray screening of artificially deformed Catacomb skulls
sources.note: Volgograd State University study separating intentional head shaping from observed trauma and ear disease.

sources.title: Paleopathology of Yamnaya and Ingul Catacomb men from the Sugokleya barrow
sources.note: Osteological study of cranial injury and occupational stress in two specific male burials.

sources.title: The Lola cultural circle and Caucasian migration around 2200 cal BCE
sources.note: Institute of Archaeology RAS study of post-Catacomb formations and locally varied links between East Manych and Caucasian evidence.

sources.title: Volga-Ural cultural group of the post-Catacomb period
sources.note: Peer reviewed chronology of a post-Catacomb group around 2200 to 2000 cal BCE and its connections to later formations.

sources.title: Continuity of sacred spaces in the North Pontic Steppe
sources.note: Antiquity case study of a repeatedly used Ukrainian mound with dated Catacomb and earlier phases.

sources.title: Bioarchaeology of the North Caucasus Bronze Age
sources.note: Open academic volume stressing burial-heavy evidence, chronological debates, regional fragmentation, and weak settlement-burial linkage.

sources.title: Catacomb culture
sources.note: Encyclopedia of Ukraine overview of Gorodtsov’s classification and finds across Ukraine, Crimea, the Don, and Kalmykia.

sources.title: Egalitarian pastoral society versus nomadic warriors?
sources.note: Scholarly reconstruction comparing competing readings of Yamnaya and Catacomb grave evidence and social structure.

sources.title: Bronze Age clay censers in the Carpathian Basin and eastern steppe research
sources.note: Hungarian Academy open study reviewing Catacomb censer forms, ornament, chronology, and interpretive history.

sources.title: An anthropological marker for migrations in Catacomb culture complexes
sources.note: Scholarly Lower Volga study joining skeletal and archaeological evidence while treating biological traits as population-history clues, not ethnic names.
